mission: Cockpit, night cycle. Desh walks Ben through the team status as a debrief: Torin is separating, Sera is rigid, Kael is watching the exit, Ben is carrying too much alone. The diagnosis is clinical until it is not: 'I didn't come here to watch another good person convince themselves they're the only answer.'
why_now: The Jacen recognition has to be met with a sentence from someone who was there. Desh is the only person on the ship who can speak this one, and the scene earns his arc-moment-of-truth.
conflict: The assessment Ben needs is the assessment he does not want. Desh delivers it as professional debrief until the last sentence, which he delivers as himself. Ben cannot argue with any part of it.
turning_point: Desh: 'I didn't come here to watch another good person convince themselves they're the only answer.' Ben hears Jacen, he hears Torin, and he hears himself. Desh does not have to specify.
opening_hook: Desh doesn't frame it as a warning. He frames it as a debrief. 'Let me walk you through the team status.' It's the most frightening sentence Ben has heard on this trip.
closing_hook: Desh's final assessment: 'You need to give them a reason to stay that isn't you telling them to.' Ben doesn't have that reason yet. But he knows where to look — somewhere in the Codex notes he bookmarked and hasn't revisited.
emotional_trajectory: Professional assessment -> personal investment revealed -> the challenge to Ben's leadership approach

stakes.personal: Desh's arc turning — obligation becoming investment
stakes.interpersonal: The group's survival as a functioning unit
stakes.external: A fractured group cannot face Veraine at Veranthos

setting: Aboard the Steady Returns — cockpit, night cycle
sensory_details: Instrument lights; Desh's voice steady and professional until the last line, when it is not; the nav display showing Veranthos's system approaching; the countdown timer Desh posted on the bulkhead, smaller every time Ben reads it
action_beats: Desh pulls out his datapad and walks Ben through each team member's status — clinical, precise, devastating
Desh taps the countdown timer he posted on the bulkhead without looking at it
Ben stares at the Codex file bookmark on his datapad after Desh leaves — the resonance note waiting
notes: Desh's arc-moment-of-truth — operational concern revealing genuine investment. The Jacen reference is powerful because Desh is the only person who watched it happen in real time beside Ben. Diagnostic-voice trap — Ben should not, in this scene, write a paragraph identifying himself in Desh's sentence. The identification is registered through what Ben does after Desh leaves (stares at the Codex bookmark) rather than through an explicit interior line. Voice: dialogue-precision; the debrief carries the scene, the personal line lands and the scene ends shortly after.
